messages.subject: Outputs ~0 for soil moisture when specifying zero plane displacement correction factor in mature forest (micro_ncep)
messages.subject_clean: Outputs ~0 for soil moisture when specifying zero plane displacement correction factor in mature forest (micro_ncep)
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I am running into a problem where the soil moisture model in the micron_ncep() function is giving me spurious results. When parameterizing the model, I have been using the suggested 0.6*canopy height (meters) for the zero plane displacement correction (D0) and 0.02* the canopy height (meters) for the heat transfer roughness height (ZH). However, the model works correctly when I omit the the D0 term and use the roughness height instead (RUF). So my question is, what would be the ideal parameterization of RUF for a fairly mature, southern Applachian forest or is there a way to more properly account for the vegetation height?

Thanks!
-Andrew

messages.body_plain:
Hey all,

I have a fair few number of spatial points (650+) that I want to get a time series of relevant micro-climatic data for. I have access to a machine with a high core count, adequate RAM, and stable internet connection and figured it would be an ideal situation for setting up runs in parallel. I am attempting to do so with the foreach package after setting up a local cluster. The model works fine for running points sequentially, but when when I try and run in parallel I seems to get problems with the forcing data being saved locally somewhere in the process, which causes read/write issues for each process as the forcing data are not uniquely named. Would a solution to this be setting up separate working directories for each worker but having the outputs save to a master file?  Any other thoughts on solutions?

Best,
Andrew

messages.subject: Re: Outputs ~0 for soil moisture when specifying zero plane displacement correction factor in mature forest (micro_ncep)
messages.subject_clean: Outputs ~0 for soil moisture when specifying zero plane displacement correction factor in mature forest (micro_ncep)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andrew,

Good question. The model is generally designed to work in an open setting rather than under a canopy. The incorporation of the 'roughness' effects is in relation to how the air flow is adjusted as you get closer to the ground from the reference height and you should think of this in terms of accounting for e.g. a flat open sandy plain vs. one that has tussocks of vegetation or scattered boulders, etc. You were probably getting issues because you were sending in values for the roughness parameters that were too large.

That being said, you can potentially account for a canopy by cutting down the overall wind speed by some factor (the parameter 'windfac' in micro_ncep is a simple way to do this) and by using large values for the horizon angles so the sun isn't hitting the ground until it gets quite high in the sky, so that it can penetrate the canopy.

Also, I know Ilya Maclean https://github.com/ilyamaclean/ is working on a microclimate model specifically aiming to capture canopy effects.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: climate dataset
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nasim,

You can certainly set the microclimate model up with your own local met observations. There’s a vignette on how to do this with monthly/daily data one for hourly data. Note that there’s also a function to run the microclimate model from a historical gridded daily product for the USA (gridMET – function micro_usa) and for a historical global gridded project (NCEP – function micro_ncep). There are lots of details on the R version of the model and how to run it, including all the vignettes, at this website:

https://mrke.github.io/

the specific vignettes I mentioned are:

https://mrke.github.io/NicheMapR/inst/doc/microclimate-monthly-input-example

https://mrke.github.io/NicheMapR/inst/doc/microclimate-hourly-input-example

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: shiny apps for NicheMapR
messages.body_plain:
Hey Mike,

To implement drawing points in your leaflet map you first have to enable the draw toolbar like follows:

# SHINY - Build map for display in the web application
  output$mymap <- renderLeaflet({
    leaflet() %>% setView(0, 0, zoom = 5) %>%   # Set centerpoint and zoom level of leaflet map
      addScaleBar(position = 'bottomleft') %>%   # Adding a scalebar to the map
      addTiles(group = "OSM") %>%     # Adding Open Street Map as a base Tile that can be toggled on/off
      addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery, group = "Esri World Imagery") %>%  # Add satellite imagery as base Tile
      addDrawToolbar(targetGroup='drawgroup',    # Add Draw Toolbar to the map to allow user inputs
                     polylineOptions = FALSE,
                     polygonOptions = FALSE,
                     rectangleOptions = FALSE,
                     circleOptions = FALSE,
                     circleMarkerOptions = FALSE,
                     markerOptions = drawMarkerOptions(repeatMode = TRUE),  # The only tool we give the user is marker creation
                     editOptions = editToolbarOptions(selectedPathOptions = selectedPathOptions())) %>%
      addLayersControl(baseGroups = c("OSM", "Esri World Imagery"),    # LayersControl lets you choose background vs. overlay groups
                       overlayGroups = c("drawgroup"),
                       options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = TRUE))
  })

Then, you can identify whenever the draw tool is used in the application by creating an observeEvent reactive to extract the coordinates. Additional things could be added into that single observe event such as plugging the coordinates into the model, refreshing the map, etc.

  # An observeEvent function that runs when the user creates new features with the Draw Toolbar or points are deleted
  observeEvent(input$mymap_draw_all_features,{  # _draw_all_features is automatically the name given to the new features created by leaflet Draw Toolbar
    drawnpoints <- lapply(                      # Creating a new object called "drawnpoints" using lapply
      input$mymap_draw_all_features$features,     # We perform lapply on each feature in the input$mymap_draw_all_features object
      function(x) {
        x$geometry$coordinates   # we extract the x/y coordinates property from each feature
      }
    )   # This lapply returns a list where each item in the list is a vector of x & y coordinates

An important thing to note is that this is not a perfect system, especially if you are trying to do multiple runs while deleting points/if you have many points. I never quite got it perfect and ended up putting a reset button on the page to use between runs. Although not perfect, it might give you somewhere to start!

Just noticed a couple issues with the code I provided. The fist one is that I would change the draw options to only allow the user to create one point at a time.
markerOptions = drawMarkerOptions(repeatMode = TRUE)
to
markerOptions = drawMarkerOptions(repeatMode = FALSE)

To edit the location of the point, the user can use the "edit layers" option in the draw toolbar to move the placed point
The observe event needs some closing brackets and I also added a section that can be modified to update the latitude/longitude values directly (the ones in the gui). Not sure if you are currently including a session object call to your server, but that is also required.

# An observeEvent function that runs when the user creates new features with the Draw Toolbar or points are deleted
observeEvent(input$mymap_draw_all_features,{  # _draw_all_features is automatically the name given to the new features created by leaflet Draw Toolbar

  drawnpoints <- sapply(                      # Creating a new object called "drawnpoints" using lapply

    input$mymap_draw_all_features$features,     # We perform lapply on each feature in the input$mymap_draw_all_features object
    function(x) {x$geometry$coordinates}   # we extract the x/y coordinates property from each feature

  )   # This sapply returns a vector of x & y coordinates

  ## Add in any other functionality you want during this section such as setting values using updateNumericInput
  ## Or whatever the input is (text: updateTextInput, etc)

  updateNumericInput(session, "longitude", drawnpoints[1]) #"longitude" is a placeholder for whatever your input is called
  updateNumericInput(session, "latitude", drawnpoints[2]) #"latitude" is a placeholder for whatever your input is called
}
)

Apologies for giving you broken code before
-Andrew

messages.body_plain:
Hi Andrew,

There was indeed a bug - the hourly infrared input is made negative if not being used (IR = 0, the default, or IR = 1), but needs to be adjusted if IR = 2 and you're changing the air temp offset via 'warm'. I needed to put a catch in there so that the warming wasn't applied to the hourly infrared unless IR = 2. That's done now on the latest github version and the problem should be resolved. Note that the data is saved without the 'warm' factor being applied, so you can change it when save = 2 and you'll be able to play around with that parameter without having to download all the NCEP data each time.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: Operative temperature
messages.body_plain:
Hi Julie,

If you set 'live = 0', it will turn off all behaviours and metabolic heat production as well as evaporative water loss. I think this will give you what you want. (I might change the model so evaporative water loss is not turned off)

Also, if you do this before calling the ectotherm model, the animal will be in the shaded scenario:

micro$metout <- micro$shadmet
micro$soil <- micro$shadsoil

All the best,
Mike
